newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norwegian stocks attract more foreign investors.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian stocks attract more foreign investors.

text.p: Foreign ownership in Norwegian companies rose to 34 percent of market capitalisation in 1996 from 18 percent in 1984, according to Oslo bourse statistics.
The bourse attributed the rise to increasing international portfolio diversification and to a gradual unification of common ground rules between markets.
Six countries -- Britain, the United States, Belgium, Denmark, Sweden and Switzerland -- accounted for 85 percent of the foreign share holding on the Norwegian stock exchange.
Bourse figures showed that British investors had increased their share of foreign ownership to 36 percent in 1996 from 29.2 percent in 1990.
U.S. players made up 30.4 percent last year compared with 13.4 percent in 1990, while Belgium had eight percent versus 3.8 percent and Denmark 3.9 percent against 1.7 percent.
Swedish participation, however, dropped from 11.7 percent seven years ago to four percent in 1996 and Swiss interest fell to 2.8 percent from 10.5 percent.
The bourse noted that the statistics could contain a bias due to nominee banks being regarded as owners of shares in the Norwegian Registry of Securities' accounts.
